preconditions: attacker influences a size/length/count used by BufferBuilder/TypedBufferBuilder to a value that overflows int64 (e.g. a declared count near INT64_MAX in the IPC JSON integration format, or a huge offset computation)

evidence.observed_result: Vulnerable build (unmodified apache-arrow-26.0.1 buffer_builder.h): Reserve(INT64_MAX) returns OK (integer overflow), then Append(INT64_MAX, 0x41) performs memset of 9.2e18 bytes past a 64-byte heap buffer -> SIGSEGV (exit 139). Fixed build (commit 16900e3): Reserve returns CapacityError, no write, clean exit 0.

real_exploit.target: Apache Arrow C++ BufferBuilder / TypedBufferBuilder (unmodified header from apache-arrow-26.0.1)
real_exploit.backend: the real Arrow BufferBuilder class, compiled verbatim from buffer_builder.h against a minimal faithful Arrow support layer (malloc-backed ResizableBuffer)
real_exploit.demonstrated: out-of-bounds write: the vulnerable Reserve(INT64_MAX) silently returns OK (size_ + additional_bytes wraps negative), then UnsafeAppend's memset writes INT64_MAX bytes past a 64-byte heap buffer and the process dies with SIGSEGV; the fixed build rejects the same call with CapacityError
